series: What to Check Before Launching a Cosmetics Brand
angle: Separate product labeling, functional-cosmetic procedures, evidence, and advertising claims before launch.
approvedBy: User approval pending — preview only. Do not publish.

marketing.targetReader: Overseas cosmetics brands, OEM operators, product and marketing teams entering Korea
marketing.readerQuestion: What must we verify before packaging print and online launch?
marketing.practicalPayoff: Separate required package information, functional-cosmetic procedures, substantiation, and prohibited medical-style claims.
marketing.coverIntent: Stop launch teams at the moment before packaging print.
marketing.saveValue: A pre-launch comparison checklist for package, product file, and advertising copy.

cards.headline: Functional ingredients do not make every claim available
body: Before print, compare the approved product file with every package and marketing phrase.
cards.promise: A launch checklist for labels, evidence, and claims
cards.takeaway: Ingredient use, functional-cosmetic review or report, and advertising claims are separate checks.
cards.oneMessage: Do not treat functional ingredients as automatic permission for every claim.

sourceTrace.heading: 패키지와 광고는 왜 따로 확인해야 할까요?

cards.headline: Package information and advertising claims are different

body.text: Product name, volume, full ingredients, responsible seller details, and expiry information must be checked on the container and box.
Claims such as whitening, wrinkle improvement, skin renewal, or treatment require a separate review of recognized scope and evidence.

cards.takeaway: A complete box does not make an online claim compliant.
cards.oneMessage: Label compliance and advertising substantiation must be reviewed separately.

sourceTrace.heading: 패키지와 광고는 왜 따로 확인해야 할까요?

cards.headline: Functional ingredient is not the same as functional-cosmetic approval

body.text: A formula may contain a functional ingredient.
The product may still require the applicable review or reporting procedure.
The final claim must stay within the recognized efficacy scope.

cards.takeaway: Check the product’s review result or report record before using a functional claim.
cards.oneMessage: Formula, regulatory procedure, and final claim are three separate checks.

cards.headline: Compare the finished product with its package

body.text: Obtain the final formula and existing functional-cosmetic review result or report record from the manufacturer.
Compare product name and efficacy claims across the container, box, and online detail page.

cards.takeaway: Do not approve artwork before product records and every customer-facing version match.
cards.oneMessage: The actual finished product controls what the package and page can say.

cards.headline: Test data and advertising proof answer different questions

body.text: Shows information about ingredients or materials used in the formula.
Supports the efficacy claim made about the product consumers will buy.

cards.takeaway: Ingredient test data alone may not substantiate a finished-product advertising claim.
cards.oneMessage: Use evidence that matches the exact product claim.

sourceTrace.heading: 원료 시험자료와 완제품 효능 광고 실증

cards.headline: Cosmetic efficacy is not a medicine claim

body.text: Use efficacy language within the product’s recognized cosmetic scope.
Phrases suggesting treatment, such as treating blemishes or skin disease, can create a separate advertising problem.

cards.takeaway: A functional cosmetic can still have advertising limits.
cards.oneMessage: Keep cosmetic efficacy distinct from pharmaceutical treatment claims.

sourceTrace.heading: 화장품 효능과 의약품 치료 주장 구분

cards.headline: A finished formula does not approve its own marketing copy
body: Packaging print and online publication need different checks.
cards.takeaway: Review recognized efficacy, required package information, and claim evidence together.
cards.oneMessage: Pause before publication: product record and copy must meet the same scope.

sourceTrace.heading: 패키지 인쇄 전·상세페이지 공개 전 확인

cards.headline: Before launch, ask these four questions
body: Is the required package information complete?
Has the applicable functional-cosmetic review or report been completed?
Does the evidence support the finished product and exact claim?
Could the wording be read as a medical treatment claim?
cards.takeaway: One unchecked question can delay a launch or require copy changes.
cards.oneMessage: Use a four-question pre-launch check before print or publication.

cards.headline: Keep three files open during final review
head: File
Check

body.text: Formula, product name, and functional-cosmetic procedure record.
Container and box information, wording, and consistency.
Claim scope, evidence, and no medical-treatment implication.

cards.takeaway: Review the product file, package, and online page as one launch set.
cards.oneMessage: A three-file comparison catches cross-channel mismatches before launch.

cards.headline: What should your team prepare before review?

body.text: Send the final formula or product file, functional-cosmetic review or report record, package drafts, and online claim copy.
